title: Savings Balances and the Cover Reserve Held Back on a Personal Checking Protection Source
content:
The cover reserve held back from a savings account before its cover counts for a Personal Checking protection source is set by two cases, read from the balances the owner holds under Savings & Money Market Accounts, from certificate principal held under Certificates of Deposit, and from card payments under Personal Credit Cards.

**First case.** Where the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00 and the owner has made at least 6 card payments in the last twelve months, the cover reserve is nothing at all, that is 0.

**Second case.** Where the case above does not apply and either the owner's statement savings balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00 or the owner's certificate principal is above zero, it is a modest cover reserve of 2500.00.

**Otherwise.** Where neither case applies, neither of those reserves is used.

**Worked reserves on hypothetical inputs.**

| Owner's position | Cover reserve |
|---|---|
| Premier money market balance of 9000.00, 7 card payments in the last twelve months | 0.00 |
| Premier money market balance of 9000.00, 2 card payments | 2500.00 only where a limb of the second case is met |
| Statement savings balance of 6000.00, 2 card payments | 2500.00 |
| Statement savings balance of 300.00, certificate principal of 900.00 | 2500.00 |
| Statement savings balance of 300.00, no certificate principal | Neither reserve is used |

The first case requires both of its limbs; the second is met by either limb alone, and any certificate principal above zero satisfies its second limb. Equality satisfies each threshold on both sides.
